theory.title: Reporting verbs: advise, encourage, warn, promise + object + to-infinitive
theory.explanation: Use reporting verbs such as advise, encourage, remind, warn and persuade with an object + to-infinitive: The teacher encouraged us to volunteer. Promise can be followed by to + infinitive without an object.
theory.tip: Con advise / encourage / remind / warn, incluye la persona antes del infinitivo.

content.passage: At the community meeting, the project leader encouraged residents to take part in a river clean-up. She advised everyone to wear strong shoes and reminded volunteers to bring water. A notice warned visitors not to enter the protected area. The local school promised to organise a separate activity for children. At the end, the leader thanked everyone and encouraged them to share the message with their neighbours.

items.prompt: Describe advice you would give to new volunteers.
items.modelAnswer: I think communities can make a real difference when people work together. In my area, there are several ways to improve the environment, such as using public transport, reducing waste and supporting local projects. Although change can take time, small actions often lead to better results. If more people took part, the community would become cleaner and healthier. I hope that by the next few years we will have made further progress.

A: The organisers have received a lot of support and hope to continue the project in the future.
